statusDetail: Coverage complete. Lighthouse was attempted but returned NO_FCP; first-party trace, layout, HAR, axe, CDP probes, screenshots, headers, cookies, trackers, secrets, images, and heap evidence supplied direct outcomes instead.

page.framework: Server-rendered PHP-style MPA with Bootstrap assets and custom CSS
page.notes: Public Indonesian football schedule/streaming directory. Audited homepage, live listing, schedule, search, and unknown-route recovery. No playable match detail existed during the run, so that data-dependent template was not coverable; its absence is recorded as a core-flow finding rather than silently omitted.

artifacts.caption: Homepage first viewport: navigation and search render, but the content area is blank.
Homepage at 360x800: responsive with no horizontal clipping, but still no core content.
Dark-preference capture is pixel-identical to default because the theme is hard-coded dark.
Mobile layout metrics: 0px overflow and CLS 0.00007.
Live route clearly communicates the zero-match empty state and links to upcoming matches.
Schedule route shows no matches and mixed Indonesian/English day labels.
Search route with query, date input, submit action, and clear zero-result state.
Forced-colors/high-contrast capture remains readable and actionable.
Reduced-motion probe still finds the infinite blink animation and no reduced-motion rule.
Keyboard/target probe finds an unnamed 36x30 menu button, unlabelled search/date inputs, and inputs with outline removed.
axe-core reports button-name (critical), landmark, region, and missing-h1 violations.
DevTools load trace retained for verification.
Trace summary reports FCP/LCP at 63.15s and no long tasks.
HAR 1.2 retained for network verification.
14 requests, 1.05MB transferred, 280KB third-party, 602KB favicon, and parser-blocking ad script.
HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, referrer, and permissions policies are absent.
The sole first-party session cookie is Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax.
Eight third-party origins include ad and beacon infrastructure.
No client-exposed secrets detected.
Logo is blocked/zero natural width and lacks dimensions; PNG is the only image.
No view-transition, container-query, scroll-timeline, or anchor-positioning usage; parser-blocking ad script confirmed.
CDP console capture found no exceptions but one deprecated software-WebGL warning.
robots allows general search but blocks major AI crawlers; sitemap.xml returns a Cloudflare 403.
Generic raw fetch receives a Cloudflare block page instead of site content.
Unknown path produces the same blank application shell.
Unknown path returns HTTP 403 rather than a useful site error page.
lang=id is present, but physical CSS dominates, Intl is absent, and inputs have no autocomplete tokens.
Baseline heap summary: 128,631 nodes and 7.72MB self size.
After 10 sidebar open/close cycles: 129,409 nodes and 7.78MB self size, with no Detached constructor population.
Same-session interaction probe keeps DOM count fixed at 70; heap sample rises 0.28MB.
Lighthouse attempt ends with NO_FCP, corroborating the load failure; no category score was produced.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT (not mandatory): compare heap snapshots for retained growth - a baseline, then one taken after repeating the interaction with `--interact` about 10x (the memory-tracer methodology: baseline -> repeat -> post -> compare). Performance.getMetrics (JSHeapUsedSize, Nodes) across the same before/after window is corroboration. If Chrome DevTools MCP is available, follow its memory-leak-debugging skill: capture baseline, target, and final snapshots, then use memlab or the provided comparison workflow rather than reading raw .heapsnapshot files directly. The package-native `heap` primitive remains the default path. This check is only meaningful where the page has a real interaction to repeat; for a static page with none, mark it not-applicable with a rationale rather than fabricating one. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Ten representative sidebar open/close cycles keep DOM count fixed at 70; heap summaries differ by only about 53KB (0.7%), with no evidence of unbounded retained growth.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: a single `heap` summary's totals (nodeCount, totalSelfSizeBytes, constructor population) plus Performance.getMetrics (Nodes, JSHeapUsedSize) give the current footprint to judge against the page's purpose. Chrome DevTools MCP heap snapshots and memlab snapshot analysis can provide the same memory distribution when available. Read summaries or derived analysis, never raw snapshots unless a dedicated heap-analysis tool is doing the analysis. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The live empty state uses a proportionate 7.72MB V8 self-size footprint and 70 rendered DOM elements.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: the `heap` summary by constructor (Detached* nodes) compared across a before/after pair shows a growing detached-DOM population; an `evaluate` probe can sample listener/timer counts (e.g. getEventListeners-style counting, or instrumenting addEventListener/setInterval) before and after the repeated interaction to spot growth. Chrome DevTools MCP heap snapshots plus the memory-leak-debugging skill's common-leak guidance can corroborate detached DOM, listeners, closures, globals, and unbounded caches. Caveat from the memory-tracer and Chrome DevTools MCP guidance: detached nodes can be intentional caches, so judge confidence rather than asserting a bug. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Before/after heap summaries show no Detached* constructor population; repeated interaction leaves DOM count unchanged and closes cleanly.

principleOutcomes.reason: The site is a simple public football schedule/streaming directory with no structured agent action surface, and robots explicitly reserves AI use. No summarisation or language-model task is part of the site’s core experience.

paths.description: Homepage entry and primary watch-football proposition; desktop, mobile, dark, raw-client, performance, security, privacy, and memory conditions.
Live listing and empty-state journey; representative dynamic listing plus repeated mobile drawer interaction.
Schedule/listing archetype covering date navigation, locale, timezone, and zero-match state.
Primary search form and zero-results flow, including labels, keyboard focus, targets, and date filtering.

findings.summary: The site forces one dark palette instead of responding to the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Default and dark-preference screenshots are pixel-identical; CSS defines only dark tokens and has no prefers-color-scheme/color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide light/dark tokens selected with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Infinite status motion continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe reports a running 1s infinite blink animation and zero matching reduced-motion rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or greatly reduce non-essential blinking inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt full-document swaps.
findings.evidence: Platform probe finds no view-transition CSS/API usage across the MPA navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-origin cross-document View Transitions with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome is sticky but gives no position or scroll-state feedback.
findings.evidence: CSS uses position:sticky but contains no scroll-state container query or progress/position cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lightweight scroll-state feedback where pages extend beyond a viewport, while preserving the static fallback.

findings.summary: The homepage presents an empty content area with no heading or primary action.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile first-viewport captures show only navigation/search and a blank content region; the DOM has no h1.
findings.suggestedFix: Render a server-side heading, current match summary, and clear Live/Schedule primary actions, including a meaningful empty state.

findings.summary: The advertised watch-football journey cannot reach any playable content in the audited state.
findings.evidence: Homepage is blank; Live, Schedule, and Search all return zero items, so no representative watch flow can start.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a truthful availability state on the homepage and ensure schedule/live data failures expose a retry or alternate path.

findings.summary: Cold navigation is extremely slow and fails Lighthouse’s paint requirement.
findings.evidence: Trace reports FCP and LCP at 63.15s; both Lighthouse attempts terminate with NO_FCP.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove blocking origin/API work from the document response, stream or render the shell immediately, and measure LCP on production hosting.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is dominated by avoidable blocking and oversized resources.
findings.evidence: HAR shows a 62.46s document, parser-blocking ad script, three blocking stylesheets, a 602KB favicon, and 1.05MB transferred for an empty homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a small favicon, defer/remove the ad script, self-host/subset fonts/icons, and return the HTML shell without waiting on upstream data.

findings.summary: A mostly empty page ships Bootstrap, a full icon font, webfont weights, and ad code before content.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes about 179KB to jsDelivr assets, 164KB to fonts, and 67KB to ad scripts despite only 70 DOM elements on the live empty state.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace framework-wide assets with page-scoped CSS/SVG icons, subset fonts, and load monetisation code after useful content.

findings.summary: Primary controls and search fields lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: axe reports a critical button-name violation; direct probe finds the menu button and three search/date inputs without labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the menu button an aria-label and expanded/controls state; add explicit labels or aria-labels to every input.

findings.summary: Landmarks/headings are incomplete and custom input styling suppresses visible keyboard focus.
findings.evidence: axe reports no main landmark, uncontained regions, and no homepage h1; two inputs compute outline:none when focused.
findings.suggestedFix: Use main/nav landmarks, one descriptive h1 per page, and a strong :focus-visible style that is never removed without replacement.

findings.summary: Several interactive targets are smaller than the recommended touch size.
findings.evidence: The menu is 36x30px, nav rows are 42px high, text inputs are about 23px high, and a footer link is 15px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least a 44x44 CSS pixel activation area for primary controls and increase input hit areas without harming reflow.

findings.summary: The brand image is broken and lacks intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image primitive records a zero-natural-width cross-origin logo with no width/height; HAR reports ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB.
findings.suggestedFix: Host the logo on the same origin with the correct MIME/CORS behavior and explicit width/height or aspect-ratio.

findings.summary: Third-party code triggers a browser deprecation warning.
findings.evidence: CDP Log reports deprecated automatic software-WebGL fallback during page load.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify and remove or update the ad/creative code that requests the deprecated fallback.

findings.summary: Crawler and indexing signals are inconsistent and important resources are blocked.
findings.evidence: Generic raw fetch receives a Cloudflare block page, sitemap.xml returns 403, and the page exposes no canonical URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow legitimate crawlers to fetch public HTML, publish a 200 sitemap, and add self-referencing canonicals for public routes.

findings.summary: The HTTPS response omits core browser security headers.
findings.evidence: Headers probe finds no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and a minimal Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Advertising code contacts a broad third-party footprint before useful content appears.
findings.evidence: Tracker/HAR evidence shows eight third-party origins, an ad script, a tracking beacon, and 280KB third-party transfer; no consent/context is visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary ad/tracking partners, gate non-essential requests behind informed consent, and document data purposes and retention.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Neither headers nor CSP provide HSTS, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, referrer controls, permissions controls, or origin isolation.
findings.suggestedFix: Set the defensive headers at the edge and test them with report-only CSP before enforcement.

findings.summary: Public content is unavailable to a generic no-JavaScript/raw client.
findings.evidence: The raw request receives a Cloudflare “blocked” page rather than GedongTv content, while browser CDP receives the application.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve essential navigation, headings, schedules, and empty states as accessible HTML without a browser challenge.

findings.summary: Unknown/error routes fail as a blank shell with no recovery.
findings.evidence: A nonexistent route returns HTTP 403 and the screenshot shows the same empty shell with no error message, home link, or retry.
findings.suggestedFix: Return the correct 404 status and render a branded recovery page with Home, Search, and Schedule links.

findings.summary: The layout is only partially translation- and bidi-ready.
findings.evidence: lang=id is present, but dir is omitted and the authored output contains 29 physical left/right declarations with no locale switch.
findings.suggestedFix: Set direction explicitly or derive it from locale, prefer logical properties, and externalise interface strings.

findings.summary: Indonesian UI mixes English date labels and does not use locale-aware formatting.
findings.evidence: The schedule shows “Thursday”, “Friday”, and “Saturday” beside Indonesian labels; probe finds no Intl usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Format day/date labels with Intl.DateTimeFormat using the active locale rather than mixed hard-coded strings.

findings.summary: Schedule dates are internally inconsistent around the audit date.
findings.evidence: The page heading says Sunday, 19 July 2026 while the selected “Hari Ini” tab is 20 Jul, indicating server/user timezone drift.
findings.suggestedFix: Store event times unambiguously and derive the heading, selected day, and API date from one explicit user timezone.

findings.summary: An empty ad link and background tracking are present without a visible explanation or choice.
findings.evidence: DOM includes a zero-size, zero-text link to adexchangerapid.com and network starts ad/tracking requests on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove invisible ad affordances and provide clear, non-coercive disclosure/consent before non-essential tracking.

findings.summary: A 602KB PNG favicon dominates the page transfer.
findings.evidence: HAR shows favicon1.png at 602,402 bytes, over half of the 1.05MB load; the only content image is also a legacy PNG.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate tiny multi-size favicon assets and use appropriately sized modern image formats for visible imagery.

findings.summary: Background refresh and advertising work run despite an empty result set.
findings.evidence: Live page announces 30-second auto-refresh while HAR records ad script, fetch, and beacon activity before useful content.
findings.suggestedFix: Pause polling when hidden, back off when empty, and defer/remove advertising background work until after user value.

findings.summary: Third-party bytes are disproportionate to the empty page’s user value.
findings.evidence: Ten of 14 requests are third-party and transfer about 280KB, excluding the oversized first-party favicon.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, remove unused Bootstrap/icon/font payload, and lazy-load monetisation only when needed.
